#######1A. Alternative regression method

Goal = regress over more points to improve accuracy. For now - trying to regress over 20 points before and after gap. 

General workflow: 

  - Write function to iterate the following steps over each site: 
    + Calculate lengths of each sequence of NA and non-NA values
    + Extract the 20 observations before and after each gap
    + Regress over these 40 observations
    + Predict values for all NA values 
    + Add these predicted values back into dataframe
  - Apply function to valleySites data
  - Calculate % data regressed in each site

Write function to carry out steps above:

```{r}
##########################################################################
# fill_gaps_weighted()
#
# Fills gaps in observationValue using weighted linear regression
# (inverse squared distance weighting) separately for each site.
#
# Inputs:
#   df                 = data frame
#   siteColumn         = name of site/group column
#   observationColumn  = name of observation number column
#   valueColumn        = name of value column
#   n                  = number of non-missing observations to use
#                        before and after each gap (default = 20)
#
# Returns:
#   filledData         = original data with gaps filled
#   regressions        = regression information for each gap
#   skippedGaps        = gaps that could not be filled
##########################################################################

fill_gaps_weighted <- function(
    df,
    siteColumn = "Site",
    observationColumn = "observationNumber",
    valueColumn = "observationValue",
    n = 20 #defining input variables
){

  ############################################################
  # Make a copy of the original data
  ############################################################

  filled_df <- df

  ############################################################
  # Create empty tables for output
  ############################################################

  regression_summary <- data.frame()

  skipped_gaps <- data.frame()

  ############################################################
  # Process each site independently
  ############################################################

  for(site in unique(df[[siteColumn]])){

    ##########################################################
    # Extract one site's data
    ##########################################################

    site_rows <- which(df[[siteColumn]] == site) 

    site_df <- df[site_rows, ]

    ##########################################################
    # Sort observations by observation number
    ##########################################################

    site_df <- site_df[order(site_df[[observationColumn]]), ]

    ##########################################################
    # Identify runs of missing values
    ##########################################################

    na <- is.na(site_df[[valueColumn]]) #vector with TRUE for all NA values, FALSE for all non-NA values

    r <- rle(na) #calculate length of each sequence in vector created above

    ends <- cumsum(r$lengths) #extract row numbers for end of each sequence

    starts <- ends - r$lengths + 1 #extract row numbers for beginning of each sequence

    gap_starts <- starts[r$values] #Extract row # for start of each group of NA's

    gap_ends <- ends[r$values] #extract row # for end of each group of NA's
    

    ##########################################################
    # Process each gap
    ##########################################################

    for(i in seq_along(gap_starts)){

      gs <- gap_starts[i]
      ge <- gap_ends[i] #Extract start and end row # for "ith" gap
      
      

      ########################################################
      # Find the last n non-missing observations before gap
      ########################################################

      before_idx <- which(
        !is.na(site_df[[valueColumn]][1:(gs-1)]) #extract all non NA values before gap
      )

      before_idx <- tail(before_idx, n) #then extract last 20 values

      ########################################################
      # Find the first n non-missing observations after gap
      ########################################################

      after_idx <- which(
        !is.na(site_df[[valueColumn]][(ge+1):nrow(site_df)]) #extract all non-NA values after gap
      )

      if(length(after_idx) > 0)
        after_idx <- head(after_idx, n) + ge #if there are non-NA values after the gap, extract the first 20. 

      ########################################################
      # Skip if there are not enough observations
      ########################################################

      if(length(before_idx) < n ||
         length(after_idx) < n){ #if there are <20 non-NA values before or after gap, skip 

        skipped_gaps <- rbind(
          skipped_gaps,
          data.frame(
            Site = site,
            gapStart = gs,
            gapEnd = ge,
            observationsBefore = length(before_idx),
            observationsAfter = length(after_idx)
          ) #and print gap info in skipped_gaps table
        )

        next

      }

      ########################################################
      # Build regression data
      ########################################################

      fit_idx <- c(before_idx, after_idx) #vector w. row numbers for 20 obs before and after gap

      fit_data <- data.frame( 

        x = site_df[[observationColumn]][fit_idx],

        y = site_df[[valueColumn]][fit_idx] #extract observation values and numbers for 20 obs before and after gap

      )

      ########################################################
      # Calculate distance from each observation to the gap
      ########################################################

      distance <- ifelse(

        fit_idx < gs,

        gs - fit_idx,

        fit_idx - ge

      ) #calculate distance from gap for each obs - obs adjacent to gap is distance 1, next obs is distance 2, etc. 

      ########################################################
      # Inverse squared distance weights
      ########################################################

      weights <- 1 / distance^2 #calculate weight = 1 / distance squared (closest values get highest weight)

      ########################################################
      # Fit weighted linear regression
      ########################################################

      fit <- lm(

        y ~ x,

        data = fit_data #,

       # weights = weights

      ) #fit model using weights

      ########################################################
      # Predict missing values
      ########################################################

      gap_idx <- gs:ge #ID gap row numbers

      predictions <- predict(

        fit,

        newdata = data.frame(

          x = site_df[[observationColumn]][gap_idx]

        ) # then predict values for these row numbers using the coefficients calculated in the LM above

      )

      ########################################################
      # Replace missing values
      ########################################################

      site_df[[valueColumn]][gap_idx] <- predictions #replace missing values in site_df with predicted values

      ########################################################
      # Save regression statistics
      ########################################################

      regression_summary <- rbind(

        regression_summary,

        data.frame(

          Site = site,

          gapStart = gs,

          gapEnd = ge,

          gapLength = ge - gs + 1,

          nPoints = nrow(fit_data),

          slope = coef(fit)[2],

          intercept = coef(fit)[1],

          rSquared = summary(fit)$r.squared

        )

      )

    } 

    ##########################################################
    # Put this site's completed data back into the full dataset
    ##########################################################

    filled_df[site_rows, ] <- site_df

  } 

  ############################################################
  # Return results
  ############################################################

  return(

    list(

      filledData = filled_df,

      regressions = regression_summary,

      skippedGaps = skipped_gaps

    )

  )

}
```

Apply filters and calculate data availability - Currently not filling gaps with: 

  - >480 missing obs (= to 5 missing days @ 1 obs every 15min)
  - R2 <0.5
  
```{r}
valleyRegCor <- valleyRegStat %>%
  mutate(waterYear = ifelse(month<10, year, year+1))%>%
  mutate(paramReg = ifelse(isNa ==T&(gapLength>480|rSquared<0.5), NA, paramReg))%>% #for NA groups: change paramReg back to NA if gap length >480 OR R2 <0.5
  mutate(isReg = ifelse(is.na(parameterValue)==T&is.na(paramReg)==F, "Y", "N"))%>% #re-calculate whether point was regressed after filters
  group_by(siteParam, waterYear)%>%
  mutate(nObs = n(), 
         nReg = length(which(isReg == "Y")), 
         nMissing = length(which(is.na(paramReg))))%>%
  mutate(percMissing = (nMissing/nObs)*100, 
         percReg = (nReg/nObs)*100)%>% #calculate # obs, # observations regressed, # missing obs, % missing obs, and % regressed obs for each year.
  ungroup()

```

##### c. Change in total annual discharge

Data Prep/ QA/AC: Extract data for irrigation season; calculate amount of missing obs during irrigation season, drop years with >5% missing data, then calculate diversion amounts:

```{r}
diversion <- regFinal%>%
  filter(doy>(doyMax-261), doy<(doyMax-91))%>% #extract  data for irrigation season (4/15-9/30) 
  filter(parameter == "Discharge_cfs")%>% #extract discharge data
  select(dateTime, site, waterYear, paramValueReg)%>% #drop extra cols
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(dateTime, waterYear), names_from = site, values_from = paramValueReg)%>% #pivot wider to get columns for each site
  rename(mainSt = 3, mendon = 4, waterLab = 5)%>% #Renaming cols
  mutate(waterLab_mendon = waterLab-mendon, 
         waterLab_main = waterLab-mainSt, 
         main_mendon = mainSt-mendon)%>% #calculate differences in discharge between each site for each dateTime
  select(dateTime, waterYear, waterLab_main, waterLab_mendon, main_mendon)%>% #Dropping extra cols
  pivot_longer(-c(dateTime, waterYear), names_to = "sites", values_to = "dischargeDif")%>% #pivot longer to get back to analysis-friendly format
  group_by(sites, waterYear)%>% #group by site and water year
  mutate(nMissing = length(which(is.na(dischargeDif))))%>%
  mutate(percMissing = (nMissing/n())*100)%>% #re-calculate # missing and % missing obs
  filter(!percMissing>5)%>% #drop seasons with >3% missing data
  ungroup()%>%
  mutate(dischargeCf = dischargeDif*15)%>% #calculate total discharge (cubic feet) going past gauge for each 15sec interval
  group_by(sites, waterYear)%>% #group by site and water year
  summarise(totQDiff = sum(dischargeCf, na.rm = T)) #Calculate total difference per irrigation season for each site/water year

## Calculate % regressed data included in analysis: 

regSum <- valleyRegCor %>%
  mutate(date = ymd(substr(dateTime, 1, 10)))%>%
  mutate(doy = yday(date))%>%
  group_by(site, parameter, year)%>%
  mutate(doyMax = max(doy), doyMin = min(doy))%>%
  filter(doy>(doyMax-261), doy<(doyMax-91))%>% #extract  data for irrigation season (4/15-9/30) 
  filter(parameter == "Discharge_cfs")%>% #extract discharge data
  group_by(site)%>%
  summarise(
    nMissing = length(which(is.na(parameterValue))), 
    nMissingReg = length(which(is.na(paramReg))), 
    nTot = n()
  )%>%
  mutate(percReplaced = ((nMissing-nMissingReg)/nTot)*100)%>%
  select(site, percReplaced)%>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = site, values_from = percReplaced)%>%
  rename(mainSt = 1, mendon = 2, waterLab = 3)%>% #Renaming cols
  mutate(
    main_mendon = mainSt+mendon, 
    waterLab_main = mainSt+waterLab, 
    waterLab_mendon = mendon+waterLab
  )%>%
  select(3:6)%>%
  pivot_longer(!c(waterLab), names_to = "sites", values_to = "totPercReplaced")%>%
  select(!waterLab)
```

### ii. Water Temperature Metrics

#### a. Data prep & QA/QC

First, extract years with both discharge and water temperature data available for August 1 - Sept 30; drop years with >5% missing temperature data. 

```{r}
valleyTemps <- valleyRegCor %>%
  mutate(date = ymd(substr(dateTime, 1, 10)))%>%
  mutate(doy = yday(date))%>%
  group_by(site, parameter, year)%>%
  mutate(doyMax = max(doy), doyMin = min(doy))%>%
  filter(!doyMax<doyMax-92, !doyMin>doyMax-152)%>% #drop years that start after 8/1 or end before 9/30
  filter(doy>=doyMax-152 & doy<=doyMax-92)%>% #from remaining data, extract data for 7/1-8/31
  select(dateTime, site, parameter, paramReg, year)%>% #drop extra columns
  group_by(site, parameter, year)%>%
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(dateTime, site, year), names_from = parameter, values_from = paramReg)%>% #pivot wider to get cols for discharge and water temp
  rename(dischargeCfs = 4, waterTemp = 5)%>% #renaming
  group_by(site, year)%>% # group by site/year/parameter
  mutate(qMissing = length(which(is.na(dischargeCfs))),
         tMissing = length(which(is.na(waterTemp))),
         nObs = n())%>%
  mutate(qPercMissing = (qMissing/nObs)*100, 
         tPercMissing = (tMissing/nObs)*100)%>% # calculate number missing obs and percent missing obs for each parameter/year
  filter(!tPercMissing>5) #drop years with >5% missing temp data after regression

#calculate amount of regressed data for Aug 1 - Sept 30 after dropping years with >5% missing

valleyTempReg <- valleyRegCor %>%
  mutate(date = ymd(substr(dateTime, 1, 10)))%>%
  mutate(doy = yday(date))%>%
  group_by(site, parameter, year)%>%
  mutate(doyMax = max(doy), doyMin = min(doy))%>%
  filter(!doyMax<doyMax-92, !doyMin>doyMax-152)%>% #drop years that start after 7/1 or end before 8/31
  filter(doy>=doyMax-152 & doy<=doyMax-92)%>% #from remaining data, extract data for 7/1-8/31
  group_by(site, year, parameter)%>%
  mutate(percMissing = (length(which(is.na(paramReg)))/n())*100)%>% #calculate # NA's in regressed data during period of interest
  ungroup()%>%
  filter(!percMissing>5)%>%
  group_by(site, parameter)%>%
  summarise(nReplaced = length(which(is.na(parameterValue)))-length(which(is.na(paramReg))), 
            nTot = n())%>%
  mutate(percRegressed = (nReplaced/nTot)*100)%>%
  select(site, parameter, percRegressed)

```

#### b. Average summer temperature analysis

Calculate average summer temp:

```{r}
summerTemps <- valleyTemps %>%
  mutate(date = ymd(substr(dateTime, 1, 10)))%>%
  group_by(site, year, date)%>%
  mutate(dailyMax = max(waterTemp, na.rm = T))%>%
  ungroup()%>%
  group_by(site, year)%>%
  summarise(meanTemp = mean(waterTemp, na.rm = T), 
            maxXbar =mean(dailyMax, na.rm = T), 
            medTemp = median(waterTemp, na.rm = T))%>%
  pivot_longer(!c(site, year), names_to = "metric", values_to = "metricValue")%>%
  filter(!metricValue == -Inf)%>%
  mutate(metricPrint = case_when(metric == "meanTemp"~ "Mean Aug-Sep Stream Temp., C", 
                              metric =="maxXbar"~"Mean daily max Aug-Sep Stream Temp., C", 
                              metric == "medTemp" ~"Median Aug-Sep Stream Temp., C"))%>%
  mutate(siteMetric = paste(site, metricPrint, sep = " "))%>%
  merge(filter(valleyTempReg, parameter == "Water Temperature"))
```

Run analysis: 

Nest data:


```{r}
tempNest <- summerTemps %>%
  nest(data = -c(siteMetric)) #create new nested dataframe with columns for site and metricName, one column for data - data entries for each site include year and metricValues. 
```

Run basic models for each site and metric of interest: 

```{r}
tempModels <- tempNest %>%
  mutate(model = map(data, ~lm(metricValue~year, data = .)%>% #run a model of temp~year for each site (referenced by "."); store results in new column called "model"
                     tidy))%>% #tidy function to construct a summary table with model results (seperate tables for each site)
  unnest(model) %>% #unnest model column to get rows for each site, columns for model metrics
  filter(term == "year")  #remove intercept term to just get info on year for each site
tempModels
```

Add P-values for plotting: 

```{r}
tempPV <- merge(summerTemps, 
                     select(tempModels, siteMetric, p.value) #add p-values
                     )

tPVs <- tempPV%>%
  group_by(siteMetric, metricPrint)%>%
  summarize(x = mean(year), label = round(unique(p.value), 2), yRep = quantile(metricValue, 0.1), repLabel = round(unique(percRegressed), 2)) #create separate dataframe with p-values for adding to plots
```

Plotting:

```{r}
temp.plot <- ggplot(tempPV, aes(x = year, y = metricValue, color = factor(metricPrint)))+
  geom_point()+
  geom_smooth(se = T, method = "lm", linetype = "dashed")+
  theme_classic()+
  labs(x = "Year", y = "Metric Value", color = "Legend")+
  scale_color_manual(values = c("orange", "darkred", "darkorange"))+
  geom_text(data = tPVs, aes(x = x, label = paste("P=", label)), y = Inf, vjust = 2)+
  geom_text(data = tPVs, aes(x = x, y = yRep, label = paste("Incl. ", repLabel, "% regressed data", sep = "")), vjust = 2)+
  facet_wrap(~siteMetric, scales = "free", labeller = label_wrap_gen(width = 40))+
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size = 11), 
        axis.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"), 
        strip.text = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"), 
        legend.position = "bottom")

temp.plot

#Save plot:
ggsave("Valley_summerTemps.jpg", temp.plot, device = "jpeg", path = here("outputs", "plots", "updatedTrends"), units = "in", dpi = "retina", height = 10, width = 10)
```
